issues.description: The review word 'work' is glossed as a noun ('an activity that you do, often for money'), but in the dialogue (s1l2) it is used as a verb ('I work at a school'). A learner matching the gloss to the sentence cannot fit 'an activity' into 'I ___ at a school', so the gloss misleads for this usage.
issues.suggested_fix: Change the gloss to the verb meaning, e.g. 'to do a job, often to earn money; to have a job'.

issues.description: Anna answers 'Yes, I have' to a question about interviews, then says 'I work at a school'. The implied link (the interview was for the school job) is a jump for A2 learners and the two sentences sit awkwardly side by side.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the link explicit with A2-level language, e.g. 'Yes, I have. It was for my job at a school.'

qa_report.summary: A clean, level-appropriate micro dialogue. The grammar point (present perfect with ever/never) is modelled correctly in a question, a short answer and a negative, and the grammar note states the rule accurately for A2. All vocabulary is at or below A2 apart from the target word 'interview', whose gloss is simple and accurate. Two fixes are needed: the 'work' gloss defines the noun although the word is used as a verb in the dialogue, and Anna's second sentence should connect explicitly to the interview question. Both are quick edits, so edit-and-approve.
